Tidal is deleting 29 million songs made entirely by AI.

Starting December 9, the streaming service will reject and remove tracks that are wholly AI-generated, and says they will be gone by the new year. Tidal says 43% of tracks delivered to it in the last 90 days were fully AI-generated, and it expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day (Gizmodo, Newsweek, TechCrunch).

Music made with help from AI tools is still allowed. Tidal also says 96% of AI-generated songs get zero plays. Spotify and YouTube Music label AI music instead, TechCrunch reports.

Why it matters: streaming services are now drawing a hard line between AI as a tool and AI as the whole artist.

Sources: TechCrunch, Gizmodo, Newsweek, Tidal, Nov 24, 2026.
